381YE Spring Equinox Imperial elections.d: New senators were chosen for Reikos and Holberg, and incumbents were returned for Segura and Karsk. Generals were appointed to the Valiant Pegasus, the Iron Helms and the Gryphon's Pride. The Fire of the South passed to Marciel i Riqueza after Vrael i Sol-Devorador i Erigo's appointment was revoked. The Synod appointed Cardinals of Ambition, Vigilance, Pride and Loyalty, though Frederik di Regario, the new Cardinal of Loyalty, died by the end of the summit. The Conclave named an Imperial Censor and Warmage, and Bourse seats were awarded. The Legacy lapsed into Grendel hands, the Sheriff of Overton was lost with Overton, and the Civilian Commissioners were abrogated.

n.Dawn: Dawnish citizens took several Synod posts: Viviane de Coeurdefer as Gatekeeper of Ambition, Ranae de Rondell as Virtue Inquisitor of Ambition, Odelina de Rondell as Dean of Laroc Cathedral and Kaywenn du Launcet as High Bard of the Empire. Garravaine de Rondell was named General of the Gryphon's Pride.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the title of The Legacy is listed as lapsed or vacated because it is currently in Grendel hands.
n.Highguard: Highborn gained the Senate seat for Reikos through Cadeur of the Shattered Tower, along with three Synod posts: Azekah as Cardinal of Pride, Adamah as Virtue Inquisitor of Vigilance and Lucifer, Son of Cyrus as Virtue Inquisitor of Courage. Zephaniah was returned as Grandmaster of the Sevenfold Path.
n.Imperial Orcs: Bloodcrow Ergot of the Imperial Orcs became Chaplain Consular. Bloodcrow Yargol was named Advisor on Orc Affairs and Bloodcrow Losak took the Steel Fist.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Heilyn Bronwen's Rest of Navarr was appointed Warmage.
n.The Brass Coast: Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra was returned as Senator for Segura. Command of the Fire of the South passed to Marciel i Riqueza after Vrael i Sol-Devorador i Erigo's appointment was revoked.
n.The League: League citizens dominated the Synod results, taking the Cardinals of Ambition, Vigilance and Loyalty, the Gatekeeper of Pride and the Guardian of Giselle's Tomb, though the new Cardinal of Loyalty died by the end of the summit. Leaguers also won the Holberg Senate seat, the Grandmastery of the Golden Pyramid, the Mint and the Assayer's Guild.
n.Urizen: Two Urizeni took Imperial titles: Zeno, Stallion's Sibling as Auditor of Senatorial Accountability and Helios Bitter Chalice as Imperial Censor.
n.Varushka: Maarit was returned as Senator for Karsk. The Stonefield Ice Caves seat stayed unfilled because it is not currently under Imperial control.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained three Synod posts: Aarne Ceorling as Gatekeeper of Vigilance, Rane Jorunsdottir as Virtue Inquisitor of Pride and Nils Bardstrom as Crow Keeper of the Rest.

t.Holberg: Irina Arkady Staryn Von Holberg was elected Senator for Holberg.
t.Karsk: The incumbent, Maarit, kept the Senate seat for Karsk.
t.Reikos: Cadeur of the Shattered Tower was elected Senator for Reikos.
t.Segura: The incumbent, Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra, was returned as Senator for Segura.

381YE Spring Equinox winds of fortune.d: Five nations had denounced Yael of Highguard's Congregation of the First Empress, deepening the threat of schism within the Way. In Oran, the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull opened and drew Asavean merchants and sailors. Sinister storms swept away roads and bridges in Redoubt. The orcs of the Great Forest, squatting in the Lower Tarn Valley, were bringing matters to a head. With Dogri Thulebane gone, the passes from Skarsind to Otkodov opened to the Thule. The Mournwold campaign left twenty thousand warriors dead. Other items covered the exiled Whittle folk in Tassato, the end of raids in Sermersuaq, and the Krampus settling into its Krampushall in Pakaanan's Pass.

n.Dawn: Dawn was named as especially concerned by the deepening Synod crisis over Yael of Highguard and her Congregation of the First Empress.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of the Great Forest are described as having fled south from the Barrens with the Druj at their heels.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Yael and her Congregation of the First Empress stood at the centre of a growing schism, with five nations denouncing her and only one endorsing her.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs saw their place in the Way cemented by the new Doctrines of the Howling Abyss and the Ancestors, though questions remained. They also gained the Thule as northern neighbours through the newly opened passes and the Krampus as a new neighbour in Pakaanan's Pass.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were among the four groups hardest hit by the especially bloody Mournwold campaign. Earlier, they had forced the folk of Whittle Hill from their land.
n.Navarr: Navarr faced an unsustainable situation in Therunin, where the orcs of the Great Forest they had invited were squatting in the Lower Tarn Valley and bringing matters to a head.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast saw the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull open in Oran, bringing an influx of Asavean merchants and sailors. The Freeborn assembly seemed less than thrilled with related developments.
n.The League: In the League, the Tassato Chamber of Commerce welcomed the exiled Marchers of Whittle Hill, who bought two streets for an enclave.
n.The Marches: The Marches suffered heavily in the bloody Mournwold campaign. The exiled folk of Whittle, now settled in Tassato, remained under Synod suspicion over their dealings with blasphemous powers.
n.Thule: With Dogri Thulebane removed, the Thule of Otkodov gained open passes into Skarsind. They seemed pleased and continued to offer a guarded hand of friendship to the Empire.
n.Urizen: Urizen was battered by malign storms that swept away key roads and bridges in Redoubt. Its magicians' Wondrous Forests of the Night ritual also produced unexpected effects across the Empire.
n.Varushka: Varushka was named among those with an interest in the improving détente with the Thule of Otkodov and the northern trade network.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark saw the hunter raids in Sermersuaq peter out, was affected by the Mournwold carnage, had an interest in the Otkodov détente, and was named in connection with the Krampushall.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Winds of Magic carried tales of a glimmering citadel in the marshes of Bregasland.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page; Highguard's link comes through the Synod crisis over Yael of Highguard.
t.Feroz: The Temple of Balo and the Black Bull opened in Oran, drawing Asavean merchants and sailors seeking the blessings of their idols.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold endured one of the bloodiest campaign seasons ever, with twenty thousand warriors and soldiers dead and untold losses among its citizens.
t.Otkodov: The northern passes linking Otkodov to Skarsind opened to the Thule orcs after the removal of Dogri Thulebane, improving relations with the Empire.
t.Redoubt: Malign storms, floods and high winds struck Redoubt as far inland as Cargo, sweeping away several key roads and bridges and raising questions about how armies can move through the territory.
t.Sermersuaq: The raids by odd hunters in Sermersuaq petered out, though it was unclear whether Savik Summerstorm had secured a lasting resolution.
t.Skarsind: The passes out of Skarsind to Otkodov opened to the Thule after the removal of Dogri Thulebane, and the Krampus took up residence in Pakaanan's Pass.
t.Tassato: The exiled Marchers of Whittle Hill bought two streets in Tassato and created an enclave, welcomed by the Chamber of Commerce despite the Synod's concerns about them.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of the Great Forest are said to have fled south from the Barrens pursued by the Druj.
t.Therunin: The orcs of the Great Forest, invited into Therunin six months earlier, found their temporary situation unsustainable and were bringing matters to a head.

r.Feroz/Oranseri: Oran's Temple of Balo and the Black Bull opened its doors, bringing an influx of Asavean merchants and sailors.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: The Feni of the forest of Alderly were among the four groups particularly affected by the carnage of the Mournwold campaign.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: The Krampus settled into its new Krampushall overlooking the Clattering Gulley and declared itself pleased, a possible double-edged sword given its association with bad luck.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The orcs of the Great Forest were squatting in the Lower Tarn Valley, and the arrangement was proving unsustainable as spring arrived.

381YE Spring Equinox winds of war.d: The Grendel quit Redoubt but kept a foothold in Naris. The Black Thorns passed through the Westwood by the Paths of Lan Thúven and, with the Fire of the South, fell one victory point short of a beachhead in West Ranging, while the Jotun reconquered Western Scout. The Iron Helms took Crow's Keep and captured Dogri alive, giving Crow's Ridge to the Imperial Orcs. The Grendel overran Spiral, seizing the Legacy and raiding its spoils of war. In the Mournwold, Imperial curses killed thousands as the Jotun took most of the Greensward. The Druj claimed Murderdale and the Carmine Fields, and an unliving host lingered in Hawksmoor.

n.Dawn: The Eastern Sky supported the Urizen at the Court of the White Fountain, while the Golden Sun and Gryphon's Pride withdrew from the Barrens to Astolat, leaving Dawn holding only Dawnguard. The unliving host in Weirwater still threatened its yeofolk.
n.Druj: The Druj claimed Murderdale and the Carmine Fields, taking all of the Barrens except Dawnguard. Under the peace treaty they now count as foreigners under Imperial law.
n.Grendel: The Grendel left Redoubt but kept a foothold in Naris, then reconquered Spiral, capturing the Legacy, plundering mithril and spoils of war, and taking captives south.
n.Imperial Orcs: Crow's Ridge passed to Imperial Orc control after Crow's Keep fell. Orc garrisons at Hengesthal advised the Iron Helms, and an Imperial Orc magistrate went with the army.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were nearly driven out of West Ranging but reconquered Western Scout. They won a Pyrrhic victory in the Greensward, losing perhaps ten thousand at Orchard's Watch alone.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns sacrificed two hundred thorns and unleashed a thousand bound dead before crossing the Westwood to strike West Ranging. No significant Navarr presence is now assumed to remain in Liathaven.
n.The Brass Coast: The Fire of the South made a gruelling march from Kahraman to Bregasland to attack West Ranging alongside the Navarr. Their general sought vengeance for the Jotun invasion of Kahraman.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South marched through Tassato, which was also the Imperial fallback point from the Mournwold.
n.The Marches: The Drakes refused to retreat and held the Singing Caves, but Orchard's Watch and Greensward Abbey were destroyed. A sixth of the Mournwold's people died from the curses, and the Sheriff of Overton's sinecure was lost.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Dogri's supporters were said to hunger to strike at the Thule, and some Branoc warriors were rumoured to have fought both alongside and against them.
n.Urizen: Urizen lost Spiral, along with its Senate seat and the Legacy's Bourse seat. The spire of Evenstar in Naris remained in orc hands, though Elos was saved from burning.
n.Varushka: The Iron Helms took Crow's Keep and captured Dogri at a cost of over two hundred soldiers. The Northern Eagle was driven back in Spiral and the Golden Axe pinned Jotun forces in Freemoor.
n.Wintermark: Dogri Thulebane was captured and his army destroyed, and no significant Winterfolk population is now assumed to remain in Skarsind. The Green Shield was forced back in Spiral, where Winterfolk and Varushkan losses neared three thousand.

t.Astolat: The Golden Sun and Gryphon's Pride withdrew from the Barrens to Astolat, where the unliving host had earlier been engaged before retreating.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South's soldiers were praised as soldiers of the Bay of Catazar.
t.Bregasland: The Fire of the South rested on the causeway east of Sallow, then entered West Ranging on the marshfolk's flat-bottomed boats.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: a Suaq magistrate from Hahnmark accompanied the Iron Helms, and the Jotun held points on the route between Hahnmark and the Mournwold.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South marched out of Kahraman, seeking vengeance for the Jotun invasion of it.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Karsk's artisans forged the Iron Helms' armour, and the unliving host had emerged from Karsk the previous year.
t.Liathaven: The Empire came within one victory point of a beachhead in West Ranging, while the Jotun retook Western Scout. With no Imperial-held region left, Navarr presence there is assumed gone.

A spiritual prism.d: After the Synod failed to uphold the Doctrine of the Beyond, Wintermark, Varushka, Navarr, Urizen and the League rejected Yael by greater majority. Their military support to and from Dawn, Highguard, the Marches and the Brass Coast was halved. The Imperial Orcs declared the matter one for humans only and were freed from the turmoil. Undecided Highguard saw its armies lose 10% of victory points and break below 1200 strength. Dawn's assembly backed Yael without a greater majority, opening optional mandates: a song bringing resource bonuses, inducting the Congregation into the Gryphon's Pride, and a possible tourney making Yael Queen of Dawn. The Courage assembly could also turn the Congregation into an independent army.

n.Dawn: Dawn's assembly praised Yael as First Empress Reborn, opening the chance of a song mandate, of the Congregation joining the Gryphon's Pride and of a Grand Tourney to make her Queen of Dawn, though Dawnish armies now get only halved support from the five rejecting nations.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Congregation's call to conquer the barbarians alongside the Gryphon's Pride is implicitly aimed at orcs such as the Druj.
n.Highguard: Without a clear judgement from its assembly, division among the faithful weakened every Highborn army, imposing a 10% penalty to victory points and making them break below 1200 strength until a greater-majority statement resolves it.
n.Imperial Orcs: Having declared Yael's revelation a matter for humans alone, the Imperial Orcs were freed from the turmoil, and their armies may support and be supported by any nation.
n.Navarr: Navarr's decisive rejection of Yael settled the question at home but halved its military support to and from Dawn, Highguard, the Marches and the Brass Coast; its assembly may also mandate a priest with liao to bring Navarri pilgrims home.
n.Urizen: Urizen's rejection of Yael ended debate among its citizens but halved effective military cooperation with Dawn, Highguard, the Marches and the Brass Coast; its assembly may mandate liao to recall Urizeni pilgrims.
n.Varushka: Varushka's rejection of Yael brought clarity at home but halved effective military support between Varushkan armies and those of the four undecided or supportive nations; a mandate could recall Varushkan pilgrims from the Congregation.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's decisive rejection of Yael settled doubts among its people, at the cost of halved military support to and from Dawn, Highguard, the Marches and the Brass Coast; its assembly may send a priest with liao to reclaim converted pilgrims.

t.Casinea: Makeshift camps of pilgrims from across the Empire gathered in Casinea to praise Yael, enduring the elements without shelter while swelling the Congregation of the First Empress.
t.Reikos: Reikos hosted makeshift camps of pilgrims seeking the First Empress Reborn, part of the Congregation that could be recalled, sent to fight for Dawn or turned into an army.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: rumours claimed that one or more pieces of the Dawnish regalia had been seen in the Barrens, taken by some as a sign of the Dawnish monarch's return.

Amend motion to construct runeforge in R.d: Kahraman proposed, and Necropolis seconded, an amendment to the existing motion to construct a runeforge in the Urizen territory of Redoubt. The amendment directed that the work make use of the Asavean architect. The recorded outcome is that the architect's services were engaged for building the runeforge. The page gives no further details of cost, timescale or the runeforge's completion.

n.Urizen: Urizen's planned runeforge in its own territory of Redoubt was to be built with the Asavean architect's help, with the amendment proposed by Kahraman and seconded by Necropolis.

t.Redoubt: The runeforge to be constructed in Redoubt had the Asavean architect engaged for its construction.

Amend motion to fortify Karsk.d: Proposed by Therunin and seconded by Reikos, the motion amended the previously agreed plan to construct a fortification in the Lestasny region of Karsk. The amendment directed that the services of the Asavean architect be used for the work. The motion passed, and as a result the Asavean architect was engaged to carry out the construction of the fortification.

n.Varushka: The fortification planned for Varushka's territory of Karsk will be built using the Asavean architect, an outside expertise engaged on the Varushkans' behalf by the Senate.

t.Karsk: The planned fortification in Karsk will now be built with the services of the Asavean architect, who has been engaged for the work.

r.Karsk/Lestasny: Lestasny is the site of the fortification, and its construction is now to be carried out under the Asavean architect.

Appoint Thule Ambassador.d: The motion elected an Imperial citizen as ambassador to the Thule, empowered to deal with them on behalf of the Empire. The recorded outcome is that Juha, the Cave Spider was appointed as ambassador, described as Ambassador to Otkodov, the territory then held by the Thule. The page gives no further detail on the ambassador's instructions or on any negotiations that followed.

n.Thule: The Thule now had a named Imperial representative, Juha, the Cave Spider, authorised to treat with them on the Empire's behalf.

t.Otkodov: Juha, the Cave Spider was appointed Ambassador to Otkodov, the Thule-held territory with which the Empire now had a formal envoy.

Archive:381YE Spring Equinox Imperial ti.d: The page listed every senator by territory, every general by nation, the Synod's cardinals, gatekeepers and inquisitors, the Conclave's archmagi and grandmasters, and the holders of Bourse seats and lesser titles. Several posts stood vacant, including the Minister of Historical Research, the Ambassador to the Commonwealth and the Custodian of the Imperial War Memorial. The Cardinal of Loyalty was vacant after the death of Frederik di Regario. The Civilian Commissioners no longer existed, having been abrogated at the Winter Solstice 380YE. The Damatian Cliffs were back under Imperial control and awaited allocation by the Senate. Two national Bourse seats were in foreign hands: the Thule held the Stonefield Ice Caves and the Grendel held the Legacy.

n.Dawn: Dawn's senators were Bohemond de Rondell, Escalados de Carsenere and Valentin Ivarovich Orzel, and it fielded four generals. Agnetha De Rondell was Cardinal of Wisdom and Kaywenn du Launcet was High Bard of the Empire.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel held the Legacy, a Urizen national Bourse seat.
n.Highguard: Highguard held four Senate seats and three generalships, under Cuth, Mathayus and Cayleb. Azekah of Zephaniah's Lament was Cardinal of Pride and Ephron of Adina's Charge was Imperial Inquisitor.
n.Imperial Orcs: Irontide Vio was Senator for Skarsind, and Bloodcrow Morgur and Irontide Skar led the orc armies. Atla was Cardinal of the Way and Bloodcrow Yargol was Advisor on Orc Affairs.
n.Navarr: Navarr's three senators sat alongside Generals Ulric Y'Basden and Brennos Brackensong. Navarr also held the Warmage post through Heilyn and the Quartermaster General post through Brendan Brackensong.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn held four Senate seats and three military commands, including Admiral Edgardo i Ruiloba i Guerra of the Freeborn Storm. Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra was Imperial Fleet Master.
n.The League: A Leaguer, Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, sat on the Throne, and the nation held four Senate seats and the Barossa generalships. Its Cardinal of Loyalty was vacant after Frederik di Regario's death.
n.The Marches: The Marches held three Senate seats and four generalships. Tess was Gatekeeper of Loyalty and Robert Shanks operated Brock's Toll.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule held the Stonefield Ice Caves, a Wintermark national Bourse seat.
n.Urizen: Urizen held three Senate seats and a single general, Nicassia Avicia of the Citadel Guard. Levitia of Endsmeet was Cardinal of Courage, and its national Bourse seat, the Legacy, was held by the Grendel.
n.Varushka: Varushka held four Senate seats and three generalships, over the Northern Eagle, the Golden Axe and the Iron Helms. Amris was Gatekeeper of Wisdom.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark held three Senate seats and two generals, Iron Osric and Erkenbrand. Ingrid Sigeing was Conscience of the Senate, and its Stonefield Ice Caves Bourse seat was held by the Thule.

t.Astolat: Bohemond de Rondell sat as Senator for Astolat.
t.Bastion: Ibrahim, the South Paw, of the Cohort of the Winter Bear sat as Senator for Bastion.
t.Bregasland: Orrick sat as Senator for Bregasland, the Dour Fens, and Bill of Middleton held the sinecure of Keeper of the Dour Fens.
t.Casinea: Barrabas sat as Senator for Casinea.
t.Feroz: Oria sat as Senator for Feroz.
t.Hahnmark: Hengest Dun sat as Senator for Hahnmark.
t.Hercynia: Ranulf Pridestalker sat as Senator for Hercynia.
t.Holberg: Irina Arkady Staryn Von Holberg sat as Senator for Holberg, and the Empress herself, Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, bore the territory's name.
t.Kahraman: Qusay i Kalamar i Guerra sat as Senator for Kahraman.
t.Kallavesa: Olle Markusson sat as Senator for Kallavesa.
t.Karov: Ludmilla Koslov sat as Senator for Karov.
t.Karsk: Maarit sat as Senator for Karsk.
t.Madruga: Anwar i Del-Toro i Riquezza sat as Senator for Madruga.
t.Miaren: Llewellyn Leafstalker sat as Senator for Miaren, while the sinecure of Eternal Flame of Miaren stood vacant.
t.Miekarova: Father Nikolovich Drakov sat as Senator for Miekarova.
t.Mitwold: Bridget Eastville sat as Senator for Mitwold, Pride of the Marches.
t.Morrow: Ariadne sat as Senator for Morrow.
t.Necropolis: Ianthe, of Raven's Watch, sat as Senator for Necropolis.
t.Redoubt: Probus of Shattered Spire sat as Senator for Redoubt.
t.Reikos: Cadeus, of the Shattered Tower, sat as Senator for Reikos, and Nemuel of Ravensfell held the Great Forest at Reikos Bourse seat.
t.Sarvos: Magdelena di Sarvos sat as Senator for Sarvos.
t.Segura: Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra sat as Senator for Segura.
t.Semmerholm: Escalados de Carsenere sat as Senator for Semmerholm.
t.Sermersuaq: Atte sat as Senator for Sermersuaq.
t.Skarsind: Irontide Vio sat as Senator for Skarsind, and Irontide T'onk was Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting.
t.Tassato: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato sat as Senator for Tassato, and Beatriz Sanguineo Rezia was Steward of the Tassato Mana Exchange.
t.Temeschwar: Gant Archama sat as Senator for Temeschwar.
t.Therunin: Willa Farkus-Vigil sat as Senator for Therunin.
t.Upwold: Henry Ward sat as Senator for Upwold, The Silver Chase.
t.Volodmartz: Vuk the Wolfeater sat as Senator for Volodmartz.
t.Weirwater: Valentin Ivarovich Orzel sat as Senator for Weirwater, and Jack Plank held the Weirwater Vales Bourse seat for 50 Thrones.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Great Pits of Ennerlund Bourse seat was held by Lukash Biessek von Temeschwar for 590 Thrones.

Construct Art Museum of Tassato.d: The motion authorised a great work in Tassato at a cost of 15 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones in labour, taking three months to construct. After the Spring Equinox 381YE Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar provided all the required materials and money. The completed great work, the Blood Red River Museum, provides 15 liao and 30 votes in the Imperial Synod each season. These are spread among citizens of Tassato dedicated to Pride who own congregations, following attendance at the Anvil Summit.

n.The League: The League gained a great work in one of its cities, the Blood Red River Museum, which strengthens Pride-dedicated League congregations with additional liao and Synod votes.

t.Tassato: Tassato became home to the Blood Red River Museum, funded by Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar, which each season gives its Pride-dedicated congregation owners 15 liao and 30 Synod votes between them.

Construct Gardens of the Grim III.d: Passed in Spring 381YE, this was the third motion to construct the Gardens of the Grim, following two earlier attempts. Once completed, the gardens would create a new Varushkan national title, the Grim Gardener, elected by the Varushkan Senators, and would double as the Courage artefact 'The Chains of Chernebog'. The exact cost is not recorded, but standard costs applied. After the Spring Equinox, Father Drakov provided 20 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones towards construction.

n.Varushka: Varushka's senators backed the project, and once built it would give the nation a new title, the Grim Gardener, chosen by its own Senators.

t.Miekarova: The Gardens of the Grim were to be built in Miekarova as an herb sinecure and the Courage artefact 'The Chains of Chernebog', with Father Drakov supplying weirwood and thrones towards the work.

Construct Grand Art Gallery of Sarvos.d: Proposed by the senator for Sarvos and seconded by Tassato, the motion sought a grand art gallery dedicated to Pride, in keeping with the Virtuous interest in the League's cultural renaissance. It cost 15 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones in labour, and took three months to build. Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar provided all of the materials and money after the Spring Equinox. The finished work, the Blood Red Quays Art Gallery, gives 15 liao and 30 votes in the Imperial Synod each season. These are shared among Sarvos citizens dedicated to Pride who own congregations, following attendance at the Anvil Summit.

n.The League: League senators for Sarvos and Tassato brought forward the motion, celebrating the League's cultural renaissance with a Pride-dedicated gallery, and a League citizen, Lorenzo "La Volpe" Macelliao von Temeschwar, paid for it in full.

t.Sarvos: The Blood Red Quays Art Gallery was built in Sarvos. Each season it gives liao and Synod votes to Sarvos citizens dedicated to Pride who own congregations.

Construct Grand Conservatory of Music.d: Proposed by Morrow and seconded by Hercynia, the motion sought to build the Grand Conservatory to match the pride Urizen took in creating the Art and Culture enchantment upon the Empire, and to foster that pride in its music and magic. It passed. The work cost 15 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones in labour, and took three months to build. Ariadne provided all of the materials and money after the Spring Equinox. Once complete, the Conservatory provides 15 liao and 30 Synod votes each season, shared among Redoubt citizens dedicated to Pride who own congregations, following the Anvil summit.

n.Urizen: The Conservatory honours Urizeni pride in their music and magic. Once built, it gives Urizen's Pride-dedicated congregations in Redoubt additional liao and Synod votes each season.

t.Redoubt: The Grand Conservatory of Music was raised in Redoubt. It supplies 15 liao and 30 Synod votes each season to the territory's citizens dedicated to Pride who own congregations.

Construct The Legion's Rookery.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by Hahnmark, the motion sought to exploit an opportunity arising from recent changes in Doctrine. The commission cost 15 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones in labour, with three months to construct. Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason supplied all the materials and money after the Spring Equinox. Work was completed once the civil service received explicit permission from the current owner of the Hall of White Ravens. The Legion's Rookery now provides 25 votes in the Imperial Synod and 12 liao each season, shared among citizens of Skarsind who own congregations, following attendance at the Anvil Summit.

n.Imperial Orcs: The great work was raised in the Imperial Orc territory of Skarsind, so its seasonal Synod votes and liao go to Skarsind's congregation owners, giving them greater religious influence.

t.Skarsind: The Hall of White Ravens in Skarsind was transformed into The Legion's Rookery, which now shares 25 Synod votes and 12 liao each season among the territory's congregation owners.

Construct The Unbound Steel Hall of Lost.d: The great work took advantage of an opportunity arising from a recent period of inspiration. It cost 15 wains of white granite, 5 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones in labour, with three months to construct, and Ella provided all of these materials and funds herself. The museum was intended to draw pilgrims to Reikos, increasing the territory's prosperity, and to increase Pride congregations there. Once completed, it is to provide 15 liao and 30 votes in the Imperial Synod each season. These are spread among citizens of Reikos dedicated to Pride who own congregations, following attendance at the Anvil Summit.

n.Highguard: A Highborn citizen funded and announced a great work in a Highguard territory, which is expected to strengthen Pride congregations in Reikos and give their owners liao and Synod votes once complete.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named; the only link is the word "Redoubt" in the name of Ella's Highborn chapter, Reumah's Redoubt.

t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the word appears only in the name of Ella's chapter, Reumah's Redoubt, and nothing happens in the territory itself.
t.Reikos: The Pride museum is being built in Tabernacle in Reikos. It is meant to attract pilgrims, raise the territory's prosperity and grow its Pride congregations, which are to receive 15 liao and 30 Synod votes each season once it is complete.

Construct butterfly reserve in Miekarova.d: Using the power to commission constructions that the Senate delegates to holders of an Imperial wayleave, Julianna of Phoenix Reach of Urizen announced a butterfly reserve in Miekarova's forests. It cost 15 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns in labour and takes three months to build, and Julianna supplied the full materials and money after the Spring Equinox 381YE. Once complete it creates a new title, the Gloaming Sentinel, appointed by the Conclave through a Declaration of Candidacy, which yields 20 measures of Iridescent Gloaming.

n.Urizen: A Urizen citizen, Julianna of Phoenix Reach, announced the reserve under her wayleave and personally provided the weirwood and crowns to build it.
n.Varushka: A new Conclave-appointed sinecure producing Iridescent Gloaming is being raised in the forests of the Varushkan territory of Miekarova.

t.Miekarova: Miekarova's forests are to host a butterfly reserve, home of the new Gloaming Sentinel title and a source of 20 measures of Iridescent Gloaming.

Construct night mana sinecure in Redoubt.d: Vitore van Temeschwar used the Arcane Architect's power, delegated by the Senate, to commission a night mana sinecure in the Naris region of Redoubt. The page records the total cost as unknown. Vitore supplied the materials personally: 20 ingots of iridescent gloaming, 10 wains of mithril, 10 wains of weirwood, 5 mana crystals and 30 crowns. The completed sinecure, named the Penumbral Watcher, creates a new Imperial title. Its holder is appointed by Declaration of Candidacy in the Conclave rather than by the Senate or any national assembly.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page, but it held part of Redoubt, the territory where the sinecure was built.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named on the page, but it held part of Redoubt, the territory where the sinecure was built.

t.Redoubt: Redoubt gained a night mana sinecure, the Penumbral Watcher, built in Naris with materials supplied by the Arcane Architect.

r.Redoubt/Naris: Naris is the site of the Penumbral Watcher, a night mana sinecure that carries a new Imperial title appointed through the Conclave.

Construct runeforge in Redoubt.d: The motion was proposed by the senator for Zenith and seconded by Upwold. The runeforge cost 60 wains each of mithril, white granite and weirwood, plus 45 thrones in labour, and needed 12 months to build. Edmundo, Achillies of Damakan's forge, Thomas of Upwold and Asael of Cantiarch's Hold funded it in two stages. After the Spring Equinox they gave 15 wains of each material and 12 thrones, and one season of construction was completed. After the Summer Solstice they gave the remaining 45 wains of each and 33 thrones. An amendment brought in the Asavean architect Almodin Oktístis to carry out the work. Once complete, the forge creates the Seer of the Spiral Sword, elected by the standard Bourse process each Spring.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; the only link is the new title, the Seer of the Spiral Sword, which echoes the name of the Grendel-held territory of Spiral.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the runeforge stands on the road leading to the Highguard town of Hedra.
n.Urizen: Zenith's senator proposed the motion, which gives Urizen's territory of Redoubt a new runeforge and an Imperial title elected through the Bourse.

t.Redoubt: Redoubt gains a runeforge on the road between Cargo and Hedra, privately funded and built by the Asavean architect Almodin Oktístis.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is referred to only through the name of the new title, the Seer of the Spiral Sword.

r.Redoubt/Limus: Limus is the site of the runeforge, which was fully funded by the Summer Solstice 381YE and had one season of construction completed by then.

Construct the Great Library of Hacynian.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Zenith, the motion commissioned a folly library on the site of the ancient library of Phaleron in Mourning Hollow, Summersend. Once completed it would create the purely ceremonial Imperial title of Terunael Lorekeeper, to be appointed by the Senators of Navarr. After the Spring Equinox 381YE, Ranulf the Wanderer provided 3 wains of weirwood, 1 wain of white granite, 1 wain of mithril and 10 crowns towards it. In Winter 381YE the Lorekeeper title was effectively abrogated when custodianship of the Great Library was granted to the Advisor on the Vallorn.

n.Navarr: Navarr's senators were to gain the right to appoint the ceremonial Terunael Lorekeeper, honouring the Terunael heritage of the site. That right was effectively lost in Winter 381YE when custodianship passed to the Advisor on the Vallorn.

t.Hercynia: Hercynia's senator proposed the folly, which was commissioned to raise a great library in the Navarr-held territory on the ruins of ancient Phaleron.

r.Hercynia/Summersend: Mourning Hollow in Summersend was chosen as the site of the Great Library of Hacynian, built upon the ruins of the ancient library of Phaleron.

Construct village expansion in Volodmart.d: The motion called for a self-funded village expansion with no upkeep, costing 10 wains of white granite, 20 crowns in labour and three months to construct. After the Spring Equinox, Vuk the Wolfeater provided 9 wains of white granite and the 20 crowns, and Sigourney Kavov provided the remaining wain of white granite. Certain necessary details were still required before construction could begin. Once completed, the sinecure will create a new title, Keeper of Berislav's Rest, a Varushkan national position held with tenure.

n.Varushka: The completed sinecure will create the Keeper of Berislav's Rest, a Varushkan national title held with tenure, and Varushkans Vuk the Wolfeater and Sigourney Kavov supplied the granite and crowns needed to build it.

t.Volodmartz: A village expansion is to be built in Volodmartz to house the vigilant population of a virtuous mine there, producing money as a sinecure once certain outstanding details are settled and construction begins.

Create title of Ambassador to the Thule.d: Proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by Morrow, the motion created an ambassadorial title appointed by vote of the Senate and revocable by the well worn path. The campaign outcome records the title as Ambassador to Otkodov. Juha, the Cave Spider of Varushka, became the first holder in Spring 381YE. The motion sought to seize an opportunity offered by the Thule, but one of that opportunity's requirements was that the post be a national Varushkan position, which this Senate-appointed title was not. The Senate was under no obligation to meet the Thule request, but an Imperial ambassador is only as influential as the foreign nation allows them to be.

n.Thule: The Empire gained a formal ambassador to the Thule, though because the post was not the national Varushkan position the Thule had asked for, the Thule alone decide how much influence that ambassador has.
n.Varushka: The Thule opportunity had called for a national Varushkan position, and although the title was made a Senate appointment instead, a Varushkan, Juha the Cave Spider, became the first ambassador.

t.Otkodov: The Thule-held territory gave its name to the title as recorded in the outcome, Ambassador to Otkodov, making it the focus of the Empire's new diplomatic post.

Disburse funds to Thanmir Hrafn.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by the senator for Redoubt, followed an earlier motion authorising the construction of cargo docks in Cargo, Redoubt. It sought funds for Thanmir Hrafn to purchase the materials needed to build docks for trade with the Sarcophan Delves. The motion passed at 100 thrones, and the money was recorded as disbursed to the senator for Necropolis.

n.Urizen: Urizen's senators for Necropolis and Redoubt secured 100 thrones of Imperial funds to advance the planned cargo docks for trade with the Sarcophan Delves.

t.Redoubt: The 100 thrones were meant to buy materials for the cargo docks authorised in Cargo, Redoubt, and Redoubt's senator seconded the motion.

Distant deeps.d: The temple opened shortly before the Spring Equinox. Many Asavean visitors traded in Oran, while some travelled on to Sarvos, Tassato and Crown's Quay. The pleased Plenum recognised Franco i Erigo as its delegate to the temple's priests. At the request of Oria i Shartha i Riqueza, senator for Feroz, it granted land in Nemoria for a temple of the Way, expected shortly before the Summer Solstice. J'zarr i Shartha i Guerra and the Freeborn Assembly warned Feroz against idolatry. The Synod could isolate the temple at a cost to trade, encourage tolerance for a small boost to income, attempt to convert visitors with uncertain and risky results, denounce the Senate's Asavean architect Almodin Oktístis, or do nothing.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Crown's Quay is named as one place some Asavean visitors travel on to after visiting the temple.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn gained a busy Asavean trade through the new temple in Oran and a planned temple of the Way in Nemoria, but their Assembly remained deeply uneasy about idolatry. The Synod's choices could either cut the income of Feroz's businesses and its Nemorian trade, or boost them.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos and Tassato are named among the places some Asavean visitors continue on to after the temple.
n.Urizen: The Asavean architect and priest of Baddu, Almodin Oktístis, was designing and overseeing new docks at Cargo in Redoubt. A Synod denunciation would likely drive him from the Empire.

t.Feroz: The Temple of Balo and the Black Bull opened in Oran, drawing Asavean merchants who traded for Freeborn fruit, cloth, wine and stone. The Freeborn Assembly urged the people of Feroz to resist its lure, and Synod mandates could make the territory hostile or welcoming to the visitors, lowering or raising local business income.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Lucifaro Figlio del Mattino, mandated to encourage missionaries to Nemoria, is described as a Madrugan hakima.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Crown's Quay is listed among the destinations of some Asavean visitors to the temple.
t.Redoubt: Almodin Oktístis, paid by the Senate, was at work designing and overseeing the building of docks at Cargo, a public symbol of the Empire's tacit tolerance of the Asavean faith.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: some Asavean visitors to the temple travel on to Sarvos.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: some Asavean visitors to the temple travel on to Tassato.

Fearful symmetry.d: The Winter Solstice heralded a year of storms. Grendel navies off Spiral and Redoubt were battered, and wreckage washed up as far north as the Necropolis. A magical storm then covered Redoubt, possibly cast at Anvil or through the powerful Spring regio at Evenstar in Naris, which the Grendel had held since Winter. Urizeni morale and arête suffered. Ageing spires crumbled, the Heliopticon failed, and floods and landslides destroyed paths and bridges. A huge rockfall buried the Cargo Road pass near Iteri, leaving only a rough goat track. Armies moving through Redoubt counted it as two territories until repairs were made. The Northern Eagle completed the repairs in two seasons.

n.Grendel: Grendel navies off Spiral and Redoubt were battered by the storms, which also threatened the rations their armies relied on from Dubhtraig. Suspicion fell on Grendel-held Evenstar as the regio through which the curse on Redoubt might have been cast.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: wreckage from the storms washed up as far north as the Necropolis.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: a visiting Holberger silk-merchant was caught in a roof collapse in a Redoubt spire.
n.Urizen: The Urizeni of Redoubt endured six weeks of storm that sapped their arête and poise, damaged their spires, cut the Heliopticon and ruined key roads. Their engineers cut a temporary path around the Cargo Road rockfall and estimated that full repairs would take a year without help.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the storms were described as raging along the Bay.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: a Holberger silk-merchant visiting Redoubt was woken by a collapsing roof.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: wreckage from the storms was found as far north as the Necropolis.
t.Redoubt: A magical storm battered Redoubt with floods, avalanches and rockfalls that blocked the main Cargo Road pass and made any army crossing it lose a territory of movement. The Northern Eagle cleared the damage over two seasons.
t.Spiral: Spiral's coast was battered by violent spiralling winds and waves that tormented the Grendel navies stationed there.

r.Redoubt/Naris: The Spring regio at the Grendel-held spire of Evenstar in Naris was suspected as the means by which the storm curse was laid on Redoubt.
r.Redoubt/Siluri: Part of the cliffside where Mount Siluri meets the sea was washed away, and the main road into Redoubt from the northern side of the Siluri range was blocked by a rockfall.
r.Redoubt/Tomari: Observers in the Tomari Heights Spire were the first to notice that the storm over Redoubt was a magical effect.
r.Redoubt/Ventosi: Flooding in Ventosi knocked a central Heliopticon relay tower out of alignment and brought the network down for a time, and a landslide blocked the path to a long-abandoned spire.

Forests of the night.d: This was the third masterful Night enchantment on the Empire in as many months. Shimmering lights led forest workers to extra ambergelt, dragonbone, beggar's lye and especially iridescent gloaming, and the effect spilled into Mournwold and Liathaven. Weak Night regio were empowered, tales of Night creatures spread, and several Night eternals were expected to seek audiences at Anvil. Everyone had vivid, refreshing dreams, and naga gained extra mana or discerning senses. During the Spring Equinox, any Verdant Bounty of the Twilight Bayou would permanently alter its target forest to yield crystal fire. The Senate was also offered the chance to commission an Iridescent Butterfly reserve.

n.Dawn: A faceless ebony knight in armour of woven darkness was said to offer a night of hospitality to knights of Semmerholm, and Dawn's forests shared in the Empire-wide bounty.
n.Jotun: The Jotun are not named, but the enchantment washed over into Mournwold and Liathaven, which they held, so the forests there were affected even though those lands lay outside the Empire.
n.Navarr: In Miaren, a rippling shadow was said to wander the trods, stealing romantic memories from anyone who could not answer its riddles, while Navarr's forests shared in the extra bounty.
n.Urizen: Urizen magicians of the Coven of Umbral Reflection and the Spire of the Auric Horizon wove the enchantment, and three enigmatic crows were said to offer auguries in northern Morrow.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the Sherard Hunters of Wintermark are noted for a similarly powerful Spring working laid on the Empire almost a year earlier.

t.Liathaven: Although not technically part of the Empire at the time, Liathaven's forests were affected as the enchantment washed over its borders.
t.Miaren: Stories spread of a rippling shadow on Miaren's trods that stole romantic memories from those who failed its riddles.
t.Morrow: Three black crows were said to haunt trees in northern Morrow, offering peculiar auguries to those who brought white stones and perfumed smoke.
t.Mournwold: Although not technically part of the Empire at the time, Mournwold's forests were affected as the enchantment washed over its borders.
t.Semmerholm: A faceless ebony knight in armour of woven darkness was said to offer a night of hospitality to Semmerholm's knights.

Fortify Lestasny in Karsk.d: The fortification required 80 wains of white granite, 20 thrones in labour and twelve months to build. Maarit supplied the first instalment after the Spring Equinox, and Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov supplied the remaining materials and labour after the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox 381YE. An amendment brought the Asavean architect Almodin Oktístis onto the work. During the Autumn Equinox 381YE powerful magic greatly accelerated construction, so the fortification was completed in nine months rather than a year.

n.Varushka: Varushkan citizens drove and funded the project: the senator for Karsk proposed it, Miekarova seconded it, and Maarit and Vitaly Grigorovich Dukov supplied the granite and thrones that saw a new fortification raised in Varushkan land.

t.Karsk: Karsk gained a new fortification in Lestasny, finished ahead of schedule thanks to magical acceleration during Autumn 381YE.

r.Karsk/Lestasny: Lestasny is the site of the new fortification, built from white granite with the involvement of the Asavean architect Almodin Oktístis and completed in nine months.

Immortal hand.d: Yaw'nagrah, under enmity, agreed to send her Voice to a formal parley with the Spring Archmage, Rosamund Holt, who appears to have called her to answer charges. Cathan Canae will send the Warden of the Adamant Tower to the Summer Archmage, Solomon of the Shattered Tower, to discuss the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, and asked William Talbot of the Marches or their champion to attend. Estavus will send Supervisor Quench to the Autumn Archmage, Maurice de Gauvin, to discuss the lost Art of the Marches. Tharim will hold private audiences with the Winter Archmage and a 'Keeper of Tharim's Throne'. The Whisper Gallery declared it would speak to Ancel Steward, a declared sorcerer, and the magistrates will investigate whether the law has been broken.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on the page and is attached to it only through the map.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: a herald of Cathan Canae appeared in the Varushkan vale of Volchitrava with a message for the Gremani, pointedly not for the Master of Ice and Darkness at the college above.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page and is attached to it only through the map.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: the vale of Volchitrava was visited by a herald of Cathan Canae, who brought word to the Gremani but not to the college above.

r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: Mentioned in passing: the herald's visit to the Volchitrava vale, with its message for the Gremani that seemingly snubbed the Master of Ice and Darkness, is the only local reference.

In the tents of prosperity.d: Druj traders registered eighteen wains of mithril with the civil service and travelled to Anvil to exchange the certificates for the white granite promised by treaty. Their party also included magicians seeking Conclave business and a herb trader. Magistrates reminded citizens that the Druj are foreigners under law, so attacking, robbing or killing them is illegal. Agents of House Cudo of Redoubt offered Urizen mages three droplets of night, which lessen a Night ritual, each sold only for a set form of payment. Naomi of the Wandering Star sought a buyer for a pre-Imperial relic found near Reikos. Walter Applecart of Meade weighed offers for a magical seal skin, and Emris Oakhaven brought an ancient knife from Liathaven.

n.Druj: Druj traders came out of the Barrens with eighteen wains of mithril to trade for white granite under their treaty with the Empire, accompanied by magicians and a herb trader, and the magistrates warned that they were protected as foreigners.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a Druj trader taunted a civil servant that the Grendel claim to trust the Druj more than the Empire.
n.Highguard: Naomi of the Necropolis chapter house the Wandering Star found a pre-Imperial relic in a Highborn village near Reikos's border and sought to sell it in Anvil, ideally to a fellow Highborn, to pay her expedition debts.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: many of Emris Oakhaven's striding had been slain by the Jotun over the previous year.
n.Navarr: Emris Oakhaven, who lost his thorn sister in the Westwood, sought to sell an ancient relic from Liathaven, preferably to a Navarri who would honour its history, so that he could begin a new life as a broker.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: House Cudo began as a Holberg guild of Autumn magicians, and its arbiter keeps agents in League towns and cities reporting on markets.
n.Urizen: House Cudo of Redoubt sent agents to sell three droplets of night to Urizen mages, one each for coin, for mana and for common artisan resources, before the Conclave met.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the magical seal skin Walter Applecart was offering for sale was said to come from his last trip to Sermersuaq.

t.Brocéliande: Tombs near the border between Reikos and Brocéliande had been disturbed by Llofir's magic, and in that area the Wandering Star recovered a pre-Imperial relic.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: House Cudo is said to have begun as a Holberg guild of Autumn magicians who emigrated to Urizen in the Second Interregnum.
t.Liathaven: Navarri who had long called Liathaven home struggled to settle elsewhere, and Emris Oakhaven brought an ancient knife from Lan Thuven to sell in Anvil.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Emris Oakhaven planned to travel to Miaren to start a new life.
t.Necropolis: The Wandering Star, a Necropolis chapter house of genealogical archivists, finally made a significant find through Naomi's expeditions.
t.Redoubt: House Cudo of Redoubt, led by its shrewd arbiter Prascylla, sent agents to Anvil to sell three droplets of night to Urizen mages.
t.Reikos: A pre-Imperial relic was recovered from a small Highborn village near Reikos's border with Brocéliande, among tombs disturbed by Llofir's magic, and a local magister confirmed it as genuine.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Walter Applecart was rumoured to have brought a magical seal skin back from his last trip to Sermersuaq.

r.Liathaven/Westwood: In the vallorn-filled Westwood, where his sister Catrin died guarding the army's rear, Emris Oakhaven found the old knife he hoped to sell in Anvil.

On wings aspire.d: Summer heralds spread conflicting stories that Hayaak's Forest of Arden has become far more dangerous, whether through conquest, illness or exile. Jaheris alone is said to know the truth and may discuss it with an Imperial representative at the Spring Equinox. Roshanwe offered ten vials of prismatic ink for each Whisper Gallery pawn cursed with All the World in a Grain of Sand, and sought to send a herald to Kyra Halcyon Spire. The Sussivari Frost Coven raised Night citadels in Kallavesa and Bregasland. Two Cathan Canae citadels left garrisoned soldiers uneasy. The starless shroud persisted except in Urizen and Skarsind, where the Wanderer aligned with the Chalice, a sign of healing, reflection and prophecy.

n.Dawn: Gossip about the transformed Forest of Arden was most common in Dawn, especially among visitors to Spiral Castle, and Jaheris let it be known there that he might share secrets at the Equinox.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: devastating magical storms harried Grendel navies off the coasts of Redoubt and Spiral.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Casinea remained under the starless shroud, so naga visiting Anvil would still feel their urge towards subtlety and secrecy strengthened.
n.Imperial Orcs: Stars returned over the Imperial Orc territory of Skarsind, freeing its naga from the shroud's influence and revealing the Wanderer's conjunction with the Chalice.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a host of unliving husks was unleashed on the Jotun in Liathaven, and the Frost Coven's citadels were raised as protection against Jotun attack.
n.The Brass Coast: An ice-and-stone citadel of Cathan Canae rose over newly liberated Serra Damata, Roshanwe's heralds visited the Lyceum in Madruga, and the Brass Coast knows the Chalice as the Mirror Cup, linked to prophecy and foretelling dooms or triumphs.
n.The Marches: In Bregasland's North Fens a glowing dome of mist filled with huge iridescent butterflies sheltered Bounder patrols, though it was found completely empty when they returned seeking gloaming cocoons.
n.Urizen: Stars were restored across all of Urizen, showing the Wanderer aligned with the Chalice, while Roshanwe's heralds visited the Halls of Knowledge in Zenith and a Cathan Canae citadel rose in Tomari.
n.Varushka: Rumours about the Forest of Arden spread widely in Varushka among the heralds of the Summer Mage who visit the college there.
n.Wintermark: Husks were raised to fight alongside a Wintermark army, and the Sussivari Frost Coven used Night magic to protect the marshes of Kallavesa and Bregasland from the Jotun.

t.Bregasland: The Frost Coven's citadel in Bregasland, a phosphorescent dome of silver mist full of giant butterflies, offered shelter to patrolling Bounders, though no enemy attacked.
t.Casinea: Casinea remained without stars, so naga coming to Anvil would still find their urge towards secretiveness greatly strengthened.
t.Kahraman: A citadel of ice and stone from Cathan Canae appeared, ungarrisoned, overlooking newly liberated Serra Damata, and soldiers sheltering there felt uneasy in its empty halls.
t.Kallavesa: The Sussivari Frost Coven warped Kallavesa's marshes with Night magic to provide protection from the Jotun, though no enemy force attacked.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: a host of unliving husks was unleashed to fall upon the Jotun in Liathaven.
t.Madruga: Heralds of Roshanwe visited the Lyceum in Madruga to deliver her offer of reward for cursing pawns of the Whisper Gallery.
t.Redoubt: A Cathan Canae citadel rose in Tomari, and magical storms harried Grendel navies off Redoubt's coast.
t.Skarsind: The stars were restored over Skarsind, lifting the shroud's influence on its naga and revealing the Wanderer's alignment with the Chalice.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: devastating magical storms harried Grendel navies off the coast of Spiral.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name Weirwater, but notes that visitors to Dawn's Spiral Castle heard much gossip about the Forest of Arden.
t.Zenith: Roshanwe's heralds visited the Halls of Knowledge in Zenith, urging action against the Whisper Gallery's agents, and Zenith shared in Urizen's restored stars.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: The glowing butterfly dome was woven in North Fens, leaving sheltering Bounders coated in alabaster dust, but it was empty of creatures and cocoons by the Spring Equinox.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: A Cathan Canae citadel of ice and stone rose overlooking newly liberated Serra Damata, unsettling the soldiers who took refuge in its empty chambers.
r.Redoubt/Tomari: A second ungarrisoned Cathan Canae citadel rose in Tomari, where soldiers alone in its cold halls reported a strong sense of unease.

Price of experience.d: The Great Forest orcs came to the Lower Tarn Valley after the Senate ended the war with them in Summer 380YE, invited by then-Senator Caerwyn Summercrow. Their army is depleted from fighting the Dawnish and the Druj, and is sustained by 50 thrones a season from the Empire. They reject absorption by the Navarr or Imperial Orcs, refuse the Way, and travel with about 150 briars believed to be Dourfell Keep heretics. Talks with the Navarr have stalled, and minor clashes with local steadings are growing. A Thule delegation may have invited them to join the hegemony. A small delegation will visit Anvil to speak with their hosts and Skywise Fal.

n.Druj: The Druj are the orcs' hated foe. Their near-total domination of the Barrens drove the Great Forest orcs out, and their army has been worn down fighting them.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest orcs claim their ancestors roamed forests in what is now Highguard long ago.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Navarr reportedly want the Great Forest orcs absorbed into the Imperial Orcs, which neither group wants. The orcs' delegation to Anvil intends to speak with Skywise Fal.
n.Navarr: Negotiations between the Navarr and the orcs have stalled. In-character reports say the Navarr demanded the orcs leave Therunin within a year and pay their way, souring a relationship that began as sanctuary.
n.Thule: A Thule delegation came to Therunin to speak with the Great Forest orcs and may have invited them to join the Thule hegemony.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: some Great Forest orcs once lived free in Brocéliande's forests, and the orcs claim it as ancestral land.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Thule orcs of Otkodov sent the delegation, and the orcs claim their Great Forest once stretched to Otkodov's borders.
t.The Barrens: The orcs claim the Barrens as ancestral forest but fled it as Druj domination became all but complete. The briars with them are believed to be survivors of the Dourfell Keep heretics there.
t.Therunin: Therunin faces a growing crisis: a large orc host is preparing to move, and no forces there can stop them or mount a coherent defence. Even a peaceful departure would badly disrupt the territory.

r.Brocéliande/Terunael: Mentioned in passing: the page refers to Brocéliande's forests but does not single out Terunael.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest orcs emerged from Hope's Rest in 380YE before settling in Therunin.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The orcs' camp here has reached the limit of what the land can sustain. Minor bloodless clashes with Tarn Valley steadings are fuelling frustration, and the orcs are preparing to break camp.

Repair the cargo dock at Caricomare.d: Proposed by Temeschwar and seconded by Holberg, the motion called for a self-funded restoration of the Sarvos docks, which had been damaged by the Grendel when they invaded in Winter 380YE. The cost was unknown and the commission was presented as an opportunity. After the Spring Equinox 381YE, Gant Archama provided 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns. The docks were completed, creating the Overseer of the Cavabianca Dock, a national League title appointed through the Bourse, with the first white granite shipment expected after the Summer Solstice. The Constitutional Court noted the motion had not specified whether the title was Imperial or national, and that as a Bourse title it cannot later be amended by the Senate.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named as having damaged the Caricomare docks during their invasion of Sarvos in Winter 380YE.
n.The League: The League recovered a working trade dock in Sarvos and gained a new national Bourse title, Overseer of the Cavabianca Dock, controlling access to white granite traded from Asavea.

t.Sarvos: The Grendel-damaged cargo dock at Caricomare in Sarvos was rebuilt, restoring white granite trade with Asavea, with the first shipment expected after the Summer Solstice.

Seize the fire.d: Proposed by Bonewall Rek and Bonewall Cole, the doctrines state that orcs live one life and either fall into the Howling Abyss or cross it to become Ancestors, with the Seven Virtues offering a path across. The Synod also kept orcs within the Way and appointed Atla as Cardinal of the Way. Preachers proposed converting Atla's Hall of White Ravens into a seminary, which the Senate could commission with Atla's permission. A Synod mandate could send missionaries abroad to explain the changes, especially to Jarm. The Sumaah House of the Way is sending Tipoa the Insightful to Necropolis to inquisition the two Bonewall orcs. This is likely a sincere inquiry that could help mend relations.

n.Highguard: Tipoa the Insightful asked respected Highguard citizens to help arrange the Sumaah inquisition, which will be held on Highborn soil at Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Synod accepted the orcs' beliefs about the Howling Abyss and their Ancestors as true doctrine. Their preachers have proposed a seminary, and Bonewall Rek and Bonewall Cole face a request to submit to a Sumaah inquisition held for orcs alone.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the marshes of Kallavesa are cited as an example of the kind of spiritual centre the proposed orc seminary would resemble.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: followers of the Way abroad are said to look to Bastion and the Empire for guidance on doctrine.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: its marshes are named as a comparable spiritual centre to the proposed orc seminary.
t.Necropolis: Tipoa the Insightful and a small staff are expected to arrive at Necropolis, site of the largely closed Sumaah Embassy, shortly before the Summer Solstice to conduct the inquisition. Necropolis is also named as a model for the proposed orc seminary.
t.Skarsind: If the Senate commissioned the seminary at the Hall of White Ravens, every Imperial Orcs congregation in Skarsind would receive 12 liao and a share of 25 Synod votes.

Sinews of the heart.d: The i Tsagaan sisters, who confessed at the Winter Solstice to serving the spiritual power Faraden call Justice and the Empire calls Vengeance, were sanctioned by the Synod and all three died. Khotol Tsagaan, backed by many priests and sympathetic military families such as the Ogudai, sent a communique to the Faraden embassy in Segura demanding an explanation. A priestly investigator will arrive at the Spring Equinox, with threats of bloody retribution if dissatisfied. Ambassador Tal'Shar i Zabala i Erigo was briefed. Jarmish ports offered extra goods, Axou paid 18 rings a dose for liao, and Nemoria gave fleets extra iridescent gloaming after the Feroz temple was completed.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named as the Empire's eastern orc neighbours, with relations described as another delicate balancing act.
n.The Brass Coast: The dead sisters were Freeborn, the Faraden embassy in Segura received the Tsagaan demand, and the Freeborn ambassador Tal'Shar i Zabala i Erigo must handle the Faraden investigator. Meanwhile the completed Temple of Balo and the Black Bull in Feroz brought Asavean captains to the nation's shores.
n.The League: The Regario Dossier, a Bourse seat giving insight into the Great Game, was appointed in the League this season, and the Jarmish enclave in Tassato and the planned weirwood quayside at Cargo tie League interests to good relations with Jarm.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule in Otkodov are noted as having been at peace with the Empire for a handful of years.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is not named directly; the page only notes that nearby powers such as Faraden may share borders with Imperial territory.

t.Feroz: The Temple of Balo and the Black Bull was finally completed here, drawing Asavean captains and mariners to Feroz and improving Imperial traders' standing in the Asavean Archipelago.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is named as the land of the Thule, who have been at peace with the Empire for a handful of years.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named on the page, which only refers generally to neighbouring nations sharing borders with Imperial territory.
t.Segura: The Faraden embassy in Segura received the House of the Five Winds' formal communique demanding answers for the i Tsagaan sisters' deaths, and its civil servants have been exchanging letters with the Hall of Five Winds.
t.Tassato: The Senate's permission for a Jarmish enclave in the Tassatan countryside is part of strengthening Jarmish ties, though it could become an expensive folly if relations with the Principalities sour.

Spear of the stars.d: With Crow's Ridge held by the Imperial Orcs, the passes from western Otkodov were open. Rak Who Speaks for the Dragons United now lodged above the Red Lantern in Void. The Thule offered three things. They would join the Northern trade network if the Senate built a road from Torfast to Crow's Ridge, and would open a trading post in southern Urdur. They asked for an Ambassador to the Thule, preferably a Varushkan national title. They offered 30 wains of white granite for the Gildenheim runeforge relics. The Wintermark Assembly's judgements demanded the return of enslaved citizens and reparations. The Senate appointed Juha the Spider as Ambassador to Otkodov, refused to make it a Varushkan title, and built an embassy by Autumn.

n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orcs held Crow's Ridge after Crow's Keep fell, received cautious Thule overtures, and could trade with the Thule in Skarsind and act as observers at any Thule excavation of Gildenheim.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: rumours spoke of private negotiations between agents of the Dragons and Navarr emissaries.
n.Thule: The Thule, content with Dogri Thulebane's removal, sought trade, an ambassador and Gildenheim's relics, and Rak revealed the names of the five Dragons. They faced Wintermark demands over slaves and reparations, and the Senate ultimately appointed an Imperial Ambassador to Otkodov.
n.Varushka: Varushka gained the ilium Bourse seat, hosted Rak in Void, and was the Thule's preferred source of an ambassador, though the Senate declined to make the post a Varushkan national title.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's National Assembly led opposition to the détente, demanding the return of Imperial citizens enslaved by the Thule and reparations for Winterfolk murdered in Crow's Ridge's green iron mines.

t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named, its link being Varushka's growing dealings with the Thule and the proposed Northern trade network.
t.Otkodov: The Thule homeland's western passes into Skarsind were opened, the Thule offered to build a road on their side of the mountains, and the Senate created the post of Ambassador to Otkodov, completing an embassy by Autumn.
t.Skarsind: With Crow's Keep ruined and Crow's Ridge in Imperial Orc hands, Skarsind became the gateway for any Thule trade road, and the Thule sought permission to take the relics of its Gildenheim runeforge.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not named, its link being the Varushkan threads of the story, such as the ilium Bourse seat and Rak's lodgings in Void.

r.Otkodov/Urdur: As part of a trade agreement, the Thule proposed a trading post in southern Urdur, open to Imperial merchants and with safe passage guaranteed for them.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Crow's Keep lay in ruins and the region was under Imperial Orc control, with its passes now open. Any Senate road from Torfast would have to reach one of them, and the Wintermark reparations demand concerns Winterfolk murdered in its green iron mines.
r.Skarsind/Southpine: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, its link being the Skarsind matters of Thule trade and the Gildenheim runeforge.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named, its link being Varushka's dealings with the Thule envoy and the new ilium Bourse seat.

Watered with fears.d: Having learned the Jotun military strategy, the Empire paired Rivers Run Red with a Winter curse that killed those who fell ill. Thousands of Imperials died, but two or three times as many Jotun fell, and more than half the remaining population of the Greensward perished. Outraged Marchers in the Mourn sent Mary Singer to Anvil to settle matters with the Marcher camp. Bloodcloak-aligned grimnir and apothecaries sent a delegation to question Imperial strategy, seeking Lofyn Ulfdottir, the authors of related Synod judgements and an audience with the Empress. The Jotun reportedly regard the strike as blasphemous, and the Feni of Alderly were also hard hit, raising fears they may turn on the Empire.

n.Jotun: Their armies lost thousands of soldiers to the curses, turning a military victory to ashes, and they are said to view the attack as blasphemous, which may hamper any future peace talks.
n.The Marches: Marchers in the Mourn, already enduring thralldom, now question whether the Empire has their interests at heart; regular visitors to Anvil face hostility there, and Mary Singer was sent to confront the Marcher camp.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: histories recall Wintermark and Jotun heroes occasionally fighting side by side against the Thule.
n.Wintermark: Grimnir and apothecaries gathering under the revived Bloodcloaks banner are troubled by the strategy and sent a delegation to Anvil to discuss Wintermark's place in Imperial warfare with its generals, priests and the Empress.

t.Mournwold: The whole territory became a killing ground where a sixth of the civilian population died alongside thousands of soldiers, leaving Marcher resentment towards the Empire running high.

r.Mournwold/Alderly: The Feni said to live in Alderly's great forest were struck as hard as anyone, and if angered they might attack Imperials or stop harrying Jotun supply lines that pass the forest.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: The combined curses killed more than half of the remaining population of the Greensward.
